title: Core sends the local engine the conversation and tool schemas
goal: CEO direction 2026-11-12 ("let the local engine take full conversations and tool lists"). Core sent the local engine one prompt string; for a request that needs tools it prepended a prose list of tool names and descriptions. It now also sends the same request as a conversation with the registered tools' schemas: `messages` and `tools` on the `gpu_fabric.local_engine.infer_stream` request, built by `local_tool_calls::chat_request` from the tool registry (name, description, and the tool's published parameter schema). The prose prompt is still sent and is the complete fallback. `LocalEnginePlug::run_chat_stream`, `NativeInferenceEngine::run_chat_stream` and `ContractCall::with_chat` carry it and each defaults to the plain-prompt call, so an engine or plug that does not know conversations is unaffected. Susi Commercial Apps' engine uses them since commercial 39da0d2 (T-CLAUDECOMMCHAT-1). The answer is read by the existing `extract_tool_calls` either way.
limitations: Core's inference path is prompt-based: it has no multi-turn history to send, so the conversation it sends is one user message plus the tools. The engine accepts longer conversations from a caller that has them.
Only requests that declare `requires: tools` send the conversation; plain prompts are unchanged.

No end-to-end run of core's daemon with the commercial plug host and a real model was made. Each side is tested on its own: core's request shape and fallbacks here, the engine's rendering and a real model in T-CLAUDECOMMCHAT-1.
The tool registry's schema field name is read as `input_schema`, `inputSchema` or `parameters`; a tool publishing none gets an empty object schema.
